baker's.line: A Geordie and a baker's boy
baker's.lineNext: In the forests of the Iroquois
stanza: Now you're a good surveyor, Dixon
But I swear you'll make me mad
The West will kill us both
You gullible Geordie lad
You talk of liberty
How can America be free
A Geordie and a baker's boy
In the forests of the Iroquois

baker's.linePrev: But I had other dreams instead
baker's.line: This baker's boy from the West Country
stanza: He calls me Charlie Mason
A stargazer am I
It seems that I was born
To chart the evening sky
They'd cut me out for baking bread
But I had other dreams instead
This baker's boy from the West Country
Would join the Royal Society

maker's.linePrev: But I'll go to the service and I'll go to pray
maker's.line: And I'll sing the praises of my maker's name
maker's.lineNext: Like I was as good as she made me
stanza: Church bells and now I'm awake
And I guess it must be some kind of holiday
I can't seem to join in the celebration
But I'll go to the service and I'll go to pray
And I'll sing the praises of my maker's name
Like I was as good as she made me
